content.title: How to watch the Final Four: TV channel, time, live stream
content.text: The Final Four tips off at Lucas Oil Stadium with UConn, Illinois, Arizona, and Michigan competing for a title shot.Luke Hales/Getty ImagesThe Final Four is set, and Saturday night at Lucas Oil Stadium is shaping up to be one of the best nights of college basketball all year. First up, No. 2 UConn takes on No. 3 Illinois in a matchup between two red-hot teams. The Huskies are coming off one of the most dramatic wins in tournament history, knocking off Duke with a game-winning 30-footer to cap a stunning 19-point comeback in the Elite Eight. Illinois, meanwhile, made a statement of its own by taking down a Houston team many believed was among the best in the country. With both teams riding high and playing their best basketball, this one feels like it could come down to the final possession.The nightcap features a heavyweight clash between No. 1 Arizona and No. 1 Michigan, a matchup that many are already calling the best game of the tournament, and maybe even the true national championship. Both teams have looked dominant throughout the bracket, and this showdown brings together what many consider the two best teams in the country. That said, the winner won’t be handed anything on Monday night. Whether it’s UConn or Illinois waiting on the other side, the championship game is far from decided. One thing is certain: Saturday night is must-watch basketball.Both games tip off Saturday night on TBS, and March Madness fans across the country can tune in with Sling TV.When is UConn vs Illinois? What: No. 2 UConn Huskies vs No. 3 Illinois Fighting Illini — March Madness Final Four When: Saturday, April 4, 2026 at 6:09 p.m. EST Where: Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, IN TV: TBS When is Arizona vs Michigan? What: No. 1 Arizona Wildcats vs No. 1 Michigan Wolverines — March Madness Final Four When: Saturday, April 4, 2026, at 8:54 p.m. EST Where: Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, IN TV: TBS How to stream the Final Four games without cableBoth Final Four matchups on Saturday night will air across the country on TBS, which makes it super easy to tune in without cable. All of the major streaming platforms with live TV carry TBS in at least one of their base packages, so you have the pick of the litter to sign up for whichever one you prefer. We always suggest Sling TV since it’s the most affordable option when comparing monthly subscription prices.Sling Blue carries TBS and starts at $45.99/month in most regions of the country, which is already more affordable than just about any other streaming platform. Here are all the ways you can tune in this weekend with Sling: Sling TV 3-Month Prepay (Starting at $49.99 - $159.99 then monthly recurring payments) Sling TV Blue (Starting at $45.99/month) Sling TV Orange & Blue (Starting at $60.99/month) The Final Four and the National Championship are all on TBS, so Sling has you covered all weekend. But you can also sign up for any of the other top streaming platforms and tune in: fuboTV ($48.99 for the first month, then $73.99/month with a 7-day free trial) DIRECTV STREAM ($89.99/month; there are no free trials right now for the base plan) Hulu + Live TV ($89.99/month with a 3-day free trial; also includes Disney+ and ESPN+) YouTube TV ($67.99/month for the first three months, then $82.99/month with a variable free trial)
